## Summary

`implement.py start` derives the canonical worktree path **and** branch name from the work item's *current* title slug (`worktree_path_for()` / `branch_name_for()`). If the title is edited after the worktree was created, `start` computes a different path and branch, so:

- the resume check (`_is_worktree(abs_wt_path)`) misses the existing worktree, and
- `git worktree add -b <new-branch> .worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<new-slug> dev` **succeeds**, silently creating a second, empty worktree for the same item while the real in-progress work stays in the old one.

`phase_start` never consults `_discover_worktree()` (which does scan `.worklog/worktrees/`), unlike `finish`/`abort`/`parent`.

## Why it matters

A driven child (or any resumed session) can then implement into the wrong tree or lose track of prior work; `finish` may remove the emptier tree while the real work is stranded. Title edits are a normal operator action (clarifying scope during planning).

## Expected behaviour

`start` should resume the item's **existing** worktree (and its existing branch) even when the current title slug differs from the directory/branch name created at start time. A second worktree must never be created for an item that already has one.

## Suggested approach

- Before computing a fresh path, consult the existing-discovery mechanism (`_discover_worktree`, or a `.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-*/` scan that checks `.implement_state.json` / registered worktree branches for the item id) and reuse the found path and its checked-out branch.
- Fall back to the current path/slug computation only when no worktree exists for the item.
- Add a regression test: real git repo + worktree created for slug A, then `wl` title changed to slug B, then `start` from the main checkout (and from inside the worktree) — assert one worktree only, no new branch, and the report names the existing path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** After the work item title changes, `start` resumes the existing worktree and branch for the item instead of creating a second worktree/branch.
- **AC2:** `start` run from inside the existing (old-slug) worktree resumes it after a title change.
- **AC3:** When no worktree exists for the item, behaviour is unchanged (fresh path/branch from the current title slug).
- **AC4:** Regression tests cover AC1–AC3 with a real temporary git repo plus linked worktree.
- **AC5:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC6:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Related work

- Discovered while scoping `SA-0MVXUGXS5006M3HF` (resume from inside a linked worktree); discovery report `AH-0MVWTCIV9008ZCEY`.
- Out of scope for that fix: it only corrects the *base* against which the default path is resolved.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_phase_start_locked()`, `_discover_worktree()`, `worktree_path_for()`, `branch_name_for()`.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_worktree_resume.py` (or a new slug-drift test module) — real git fixtures.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — resume semantics wording.

# Goal

Add the failing-first regression test that proves parent AC2: during the
post-push phase of an implement run the work item is **not** a valid audit
candidate, and it becomes one only after the run's final lifecycle action.

Part of parent **SA-0MVWFPI31000HP3H** (Only mark as complete when fully complete).
Test-first: this test is written and observed to **fail** against the current
`phase_finish` before the implementation item changes behaviour.

## Context

The race: `phase_finish` writes `completed`/`in_review` and releases the
assignee inside its `StatusLifecycle` block, then returns; `SKILL.md` Step 9
still requires the read-only post-push verification, worktree cleanup and the
completion comment afterwards. The herdr downtime dispatcher's
`selectAuditCandidate` (ContextHub `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.selection.ts`)
excludes only soft-deleted, freshly-audited, child, producer-review and
**assignee-held** items, so the item is dispatchable the moment `finish` exits.

## Scope

`skill/implement/tests/` only — one new test module. **No production behaviour
change** (that is the implementation item's job).

## Work

1. Follow the stub/runner harness style of
   `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py`: patch the external
   boundaries (git, build runner, gate suite, worktree removal, the `wl`/
   `StatusLifecycle` store) and assert on observable outcomes — the recorded
   lifecycle calls, the store writes in order, and the returned report.
2. Model audit candidacy with a small, documented, test-local predicate that
   mirrors the dispatcher's documented filters (soft-delete, audit freshness,
   `parentId`, `needsProducerReview`, assignee hold, recency window), with a
   comment naming the ContextHub source. **Do not re-implement `implement.py`
   logic** — drive the real `phase_finish`.
3. Assert the ordering: record every store write and every post-push step
   (post-push verification, completion comment, cleanup) in a single ordered
   timeline, then assert that the item is not an audit candidate at each
   intermediate checkpoint and becomes one exactly once, after the final
   lifecycle action.
4. Assert the terminal write is the last lifecycle write and that the
   terminal-status read-back assertion ran after it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A new test module under `skill/implement/tests/` exercises the real `phase_finish` state machine with only external boundaries patched, and contains no re-implementation of implement-phase logic.
2. The test builds one ordered timeline of store writes and post-push steps and asserts the item is not an audit candidate at every checkpoint before the final lifecycle action; a failure message names the offending checkpoint.
3. The test asserts the item becomes an audit candidate exactly once — after the final lifecycle action — and remains one afterwards.
4. The test asserts the final store state is `completed`/`in_review` with an empty assignee, and that `_assert_terminal_status` read-back ran after the terminal write.
5. The test fails against the current implementation for the documented reason (premature terminal transition / early assignee release); the observed failure output is recorded in a comment on this item.
6. The test passes once the implementation item lands, with no weakening of the assertions (verified by re-running it in that item).
7. The test file follows the shared test-writing guidelines (`skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`) — no self-referential simulation, no duplicate of existing core coverage.

8. **Parent AC trace (parent AC2).** **Observable audit-dispatch hold.** A regression test proves that during the post-push phase the item is not a valid audit candidate (non-empty assignee and/or non-`in_review` state), and that it becomes a valid candidate only after the final lifecycle step. The test exercises the real `implement.py` state machine (not a re-implementation) and asserts the transition ordering.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` (harness reference)
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_finalisation_ordering.py` (new module)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (read only — `phase_finish`, `_assert_terminal_status`)
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`

## Definition of Done

- New test module committed in the worktree with the observed pre-fix failure
  recorded on this item.
- UK English throughout.

# Goal

Make `phase_finish` return only when the implement run is **fully complete**:
the post-push verification, the completion comment and the worktree cleanup
all happen *before* the terminal `completed`/`in_review` write and the assignee
release, which become the run's last lifecycle action.

Part of parent **SA-0MVWFPI31000HP3H** (Only mark as complete when fully complete).
Implements the design recorded by the decision item; satisfied by the
regression-test item's test, unweakened.

## Context

Parent AC1: no `completed`/`in_review` + cleared-assignee state may be
observable while any implement-run step remains. Parent AC2 requires the
observable hold proven by the regression test. Parent constraints: preserve the
assignee-hold convention and release-by-default (SA-0MVVEDK2Q008NDUH /
SA-0MVVF6OJY000JZBL), preserve the terminal-status read-back guarantee
(`_assert_terminal_status`, OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58), preserve idempotence and
recovery, and do not change the herdr dispatcher.

## Scope

`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (plus the minimum test updates the
ordering change genuinely requires). Docs are a separate item.

## Work

1. Implement the design recorded by the decision item (recommended default:
   verify-then-transition, unless the recorded decision says otherwise).
2. Move the read-only post-push full-suite verification (today `SKILL.md`
   Step 9's `run_tests.py --summary --suite all --json` cache-only check — it
   must **not** start a suite run) into `phase_finish` ahead of the
   `StatusLifecycle` exit, and record the verdict in the finish report
   (e.g. `report["steps"]["post_push_verification"]`).
3. Move the commit-hash completion comment into `phase_finish` ahead of the
   terminal write, preserving the audit-freshness ordering rule (comment before
   any audit persistence; SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM).
4. Keep process cleanup and worktree removal ahead of the terminal write on the
   non-deferred path. The deferred path (driven child session, `--keep-worktree`)
   stays deferred: document in a code comment that ownership of that cleanup
   passed to the driver/caller and it is therefore not a remaining run step.
5. Keep the terminal write and the `_assert_terminal_status` read-back as the
   last two lifecycle actions, in that order; the read-back must still fail
   loudly when the write does not stick, on both the push-with-diff and the
   no-op-push paths.
6. Handle a red or missing post-push verification verdict after a successful
   push: record the verdict in the report and in a work-item comment, refuse
   the terminal transition (item released to `open` with the assignee cleared
   and the pushed commit named), route the failure through the triage helper,
   and never revert or force-remove the pushed commit. A re-run of `finish`
   must converge (see the interruption item).
7. Preserve unchanged: push and post-push ancestry assertions, the
   per-repository finish lock, the main-checkout guard, the no-diff/no-op-push
   path, and every abort/safety-reset path.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `phase_finish` performs, in order: post-push verification, completion comment, cleanup/worktree removal, terminal write, terminal-status read-back; each step is recorded in the finish report.
2. No `completed`/`in_review` + empty-assignee state is observable at any point while a required run step remains — proven by the regression-test item's test, unweakened (paste the passing run's summary in a comment).
3. The completion comment carries the pushed commit hash and is posted before the terminal write.
4. A red or missing post-push verification verdict after a successful push refuses the terminal transition: the item ends `open` with an empty assignee, a comment names the retained state and the pushed commit, a triage work item is created for the failure, and the pushed commit is neither reverted nor force-removed.
5. `_assert_terminal_status` still runs after the terminal write on both the push-with-diff and the no-op-push paths and still fails loudly when the store does not hold the terminal transition.
6. The assignee is released only with the terminal write (never earlier), and a producer hold the run does not own is never wiped (SA-0MVVF6OJY000JZBL).
7. Existing finish tests (`test_finish_no_diff_status.py`, `test_finish_gate_abort.py`, `test_finish_deferred_worktree_removal.py`, `test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py`, `test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py`, `test_finish_gate_*`) pass; any test updated because the ordering intentionally changed is named and the change explained in a comment on this item.
8. Build → changed-scope test → commit order is followed, and the commit hash is recorded on this item and on the parent.

9. **Parent AC trace (parent AC1).** **No premature terminal transition.** The implement skill must not make an item observable as `completed`/`in_review` with a cleared assignee while any implement-run step remains to be performed. Concretely: while the session is still doing post-push verification, worktree cleanup, or the completion comment, the item is either still `in_progress` with the assignee held, or otherwise excluded from audit dispatch by an explicit, documented hold. The terminal transition and assignee release happen only as the implement run's last lifecycle action.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`phase_finish`, `_assert_terminal_status`, push/ancestry assertions, `_should_defer_worktree_removal`)
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_deferred_worktree_removal.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_finalisation_ordering.py` (from the regression-test item)
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (read-only `--summary` cache check)
- `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py`

## Definition of Done

- Regression test green, existing finish tests green, build green.
- Post-push verification and completion comment now run inside `finish`; no
  required run step remains after `finish` returns except driver-/caller-owned
  worktree cleanup.
- UK English throughout.

# Goal

Guarantee that an implement run interrupted before its final lifecycle action
leaves the item in a non-terminal, non-audit-ready state (`open`/`in_progress`)
with the held assignee cleared or reclaimable and a comment/read-back naming
the retained state — and that a re-run converges — satisfying parent AC3.

Part of parent **SA-0MVWFPI31000HP3H** (Only mark as complete when fully complete).

## Context

Parent AC3: an interrupted run must never be stuck in `completed`/`in_review`
for work that did not finish, and the existing abort/safety-reset paths must
keep passing their tests. Parent constraints: never strand a worktree or a
held item; preserve idempotence/recovery; do not weaken the assignee-hold
convention.

## Scope

`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` interruption/recovery paths and their
tests.

## Work

1. Audit every interruption path: `_handle_signal_cleanup` /
   `_safety_reset_if_in_progress`, `phase_abort`, the `RuntimeError` handler in
   `phase_finish`, and drive reconciliation (`_finalise_stranded_child`, the
   drive failure-recovery tiers).
2. Ensure each path leaves the item `open` (or `in_progress` and reclaimable)
   with the assignee cleared, and never `completed`/`in_review` when a required
   step did not run.
3. Record a comment (or an explicit report field plus a comment) that names the
   retained state: status, stage, whether the assignee was cleared, the pushed
   commit hash when the push already happened, and the command that resumes.
4. Prove re-running `finish` after an interruption converges: no duplicated
   completion comment, no duplicate terminal transition, no stranded worktree,
   no lingering hold — reusing the existing no-diff/no-op-push and push-recovery
   paths rather than adding a new state machine.
5. Add tests for the interruption and convergence paths, following the
   existing finish harness style.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An interruption after a successful push but before the final lifecycle write leaves status `open` (or `in_progress`), never `completed`/`in_review`, with an empty assignee.
2. The interruption records a comment (or report field plus comment) naming the retained state, the pushed commit hash and the resume command.
3. A SIGTERM/SIGINT interruption keeps the existing safety-reset behaviour: status reset to `open`, assignee cleared, worktree not stranded.
4. Re-running `finish` after an interruption converges to `completed`/`in_review` with the assignee released, without duplicating the completion comment or the terminal transition.
5. New tests cover the interrupted-after-push path, the SIGTERM cleanup path and the re-run convergence; all existing abort, safety-reset, deferred-worktree-removal and finish tests pass unchanged.
6. No interruption path leaves a work item claimed with a non-empty assignee in a non-terminal state without a recorded, documented reclamation path.

7. **Parent AC trace (parent AC3).** **Recoverable interruption.** An implement run interrupted before its final step leaves the item in a non-terminal, non-audit-ready state (`in_progress`/`open`) with the held assignee cleared or reclaimable, plus a comment/read-back that names the retained state — never stuck permanently in `completed`/`in_review` for work that did not finish. Existing abort/safety-reset paths keep passing their tests.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`_handle_signal_cleanup`, `_signal_handler`, `_safety_reset_if_in_progress`, `phase_abort`, `phase_finish` exception handler, `_finalise_stranded_child`)
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_interruption_recovery.py` (new module)
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (read only — release semantics)

## Definition of Done

- New interruption/convergence tests green, existing abort/safety-reset tests
  green, build green.
- Commit hash recorded on this item and on the parent.

**Parent:** SA-0MVWMUBP10041CSM — Finish main-checkout guard: failure-path verification + cross-checkout attribution (covers parent AC1 implementation half, AC5).

**Blocked by** the sibling test item "Regression tests: guard verifies on failure paths" (test-first).

## Problem

The guard snapshots the main checkout at Step 0.75 and verifies only at `pre_push` and `pre_worktree_removal`. Every pre-push abort (build failure, gate failure in JSON mode, retries exhausted, interactive user abort) returns before either verify point, so `verifies` is `[]` and foreign deletions in the main checkout go unreported (2026-10-31: 37 deletions, `verifies: []`).

## Scope

Introduce one failure-path helper in `phase_finish` and call it from every pre-push abort path:

- `_record_main_checkout_verify(stage, *, aborting: bool)` — runs `_verify_main_checkout` with the failure stage label (`build_failure`, `gate_failure`, `user_abort`, `refactor`), and when violations are found posts the loud `_main_checkout_guard_message` via `wl_add_comment` (naming every path, the actor evidence and the recovery command) **in addition to** the existing failure comment — never instead of it (fail loud, never silent).
- Wire it into: Step 2 build failure; Step 3 gate failure in `json_output` mode; Step 3 retries exhausted; Step 3 interactive `abort` choice.
- `guard["verdict"]` becomes `fail` when a failure-path verify finds violations, so the report is honest even though those paths already return without raising.
- **Refactor step (advisory):** `run_refactor` failure currently only logs a warning and continues. Record a `refactor` verify entry **report-only** — a violation found there is surfaced in the report and in a wl comment but does not abort, preserving today's non-gating refactor semantics. Document this decision in the code comment and in the item comment.
- Expose the verify stage list in the report docstring/constant so the docs item can reference it (`VERIFY_STAGES`-style constant or module docstring).

**Parent ACs restated verbatim below** (the plan's AC coverage review measures similarity against them); this item's own checks follow.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Failure-path verification.** When finish aborts before the push (gate failure, build failure, refactor failure, user abort) and the main-checkout snapshot shows foreign changes (deletions especially), the guard reports them loudly — naming every path and the concurrent-actor evidence — via a wl comment on the work item, leaving the item open. A regression test covers a foreign-deletion abort at the gate stage (`verifies` non-empty on failure paths).
- **No regression on benign concurrent churn.** All changed-scope tests pass; the finish gate stays green for a clean run (no false positives on benign concurrent churn — the SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG defect class must not regress).
- Build failure, gate failure (JSON mode), retries-exhausted and interactive user abort each append a verify entry naming the failure stage, so `verifies` is never empty on a pre-push abort.
- When a failure-path verify finds foreign paths, a wl comment names every offending path, the actor evidence and the recovery command, and the pre-existing failure comment is still posted (both comments, in order).
- `report["steps"]["main_checkout_guard"]["verdict"] == "fail"` whenever any verify entry fails, including failure-path entries; the report is emitted with the failure verdict on the early-return paths.
- The work item is left `open` on every abort path (unchanged), and no failure-path verify introduces a new abort for benign concurrent churn — a clean failure path keeps `verdict == "pass"`.
- The refactor verify never aborts a run; its advisory status is documented in the code comment and recorded as a comment on this item.
- All new tests from the sibling test item pass; changed-scope gate green via `/skill:test`.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` Steps 1–3, `_abort_on_main_checkout_violation`, `_verify_main_checkout`, `_main_checkout_guard_message`.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py` — tests written by the sibling item.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — guard section updated by the docs item; keep the code comments here in sync.

## Documented assumption

Refactor failure is advisory today (`LOG.warning` + continue), so it is not an abort path; the guard verifies there report-only rather than turning a pre-existing advisory step into a new abort source (false-positive risk under parent AC5). Deviation from the parent brief's "refactor failure" abort list is deliberate and recorded.

## Goal

As a producer/agent, I want a single, reproducible per-test-file **keep / rework / prune** verdict that combines churn, mutation, anti-pattern and runtime evidence, so test-value decisions are made from one reconciled report rather than four separate reads.

## Problem statement

Today the evidence for test value is fragmented across `skill/test-churn` (evolution/growth), the mutation-testing campaign (`SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O`, fault detection), `evaluate_usefulness.py` + `test-writing-guidelines.md` (static anti-patterns) and the test runner (runtime/flake). Each answers a different question; none produces an auditable per-file verdict. Epic `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` needs a repeatable classify → prove → report pipeline, and this skill is the missing connective tissue between those signals.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Ingests, per test file: churn metrics (rewrite/growth/stability), mutation score, anti-pattern verdicts, and runtime/flake data when available.
- [ ] Emits one verdict per file — `keep`, `rework` or `prune` — with the evidence for that verdict recorded.
- [ ] Totals reconcile: verdict counts sum to files in scope, and every verdict cites at least one evidence source.
- [ ] Produces `test_value_report.md` + `test_value_data.json` with documented definitions and limitations.
- [ ] Orchestrates the existing analysers; it does not reimplement churn, mutation or anti-pattern detection.
- [ ] Missing inputs degrade honestly (the report states which signals were absent; it never fabricates a verdict).
- [ ] Reproducible (pinned inputs, documented command, deterministic ordering) and covered by tests.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Read-only against the analysed project.
- Must not turn a heuristic into an automatic deletion; `prune` is advisory and conservative.
- No per-project hardcoded paths; project root is an argument.
- Follows the repository skill contract and `$(skill_path ...)` shared-library resolution.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — test-value refactor epic (classify/prove/report).
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing on top-churn modules (behavioural evidence arm).
- `skill/test-churn`, `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`, `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`.

**Parent:** SA-0MVWMUBP10041CSM — Finish main-checkout guard: failure-path verification + cross-checkout attribution (covers parent AC2, AC3 implementation halves).

**Blocked by** the sibling test item "Regression tests: cross-checkout attribution and fail-closed repo_root" (test-first).

## Problem

Two attribution defects:

1. `_resolve_main_repo_root` trusts `state.repo_root` whenever it is not the worktree or inside it, so a state file pointing at a sibling checkout makes finish snapshot, fast-forward and push a foreign repository.
2. `_record_finish_own_churn` returns the raw `git diff --name-only before after` list from `repo_root`; nothing constrains those paths to the repo being finished or to churn actually observed in that checkout, and `_main_checkout_guard_violations` allow-lists any listed path with a non-deletion code.

## Scope

- **Fail-closed `repo_root`.** In `_resolve_main_repo_root`, derive `main = _get_repo_root(worktree_path)` (git common dir parent) and require `state.repo_root` to resolve to that same root. On mismatch: log a loud WARNING naming the rejected and derived roots and use the derived root — never the stated foreign value. Keep the existing stale-state rejection, and keep the current fallback (stated root, or cwd discovery) only when derivation is impossible (`_get_repo_root` returns `None`), with a warning. Never return a path outside the repo that owns the worktree.
- **Constrained `own_churn`.** In `_record_finish_own_churn`: resolve `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and `--git-common-dir` for `repo_root` and refuse (return `[]` + warning) when they disagree with `repo_root`; drop every path that is absolute, contains `..`, or does not resolve inside `repo_root`; and intersect the diff list with the paths actually observed dirty in the finished checkout (pass the post-fast-forward snapshot in, or re-snapshot inside the helper). Report dropped/not-observed paths as a `not_observed` diagnostic in `report["steps"]["local_dev_fast_forward"]` — visible, never allow-listed.
- Only record `own_churn` when the fast-forward actually advanced the checkout (`method == "advanced"`); a refused/no-op fast-forward contributes an empty list.
- Keep the invariant that a deletion (`D`) is never allow-listed, and keep SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG's benign-concurrent-churn exclusion intact (no new false positives for a clean run).
- Document the contract in the affected docstrings (`_resolve_main_repo_root`, `_record_finish_own_churn`, `_main_checkout_guard_violations`).

**Parent ACs restated verbatim below** (the plan's AC coverage review measures similarity against them); this item's own checks follow.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Attribution correctness.** `own_churn` never lists paths belonging to another checkout/repo, and the guard's `repo_root` resolution can never resolve to, or act on, a path outside its own repo. A test asserts foreign paths are not allow-listed and are reported as violations instead.
- `_resolve_main_repo_root` returns the main checkout derived from the worktree whenever that is derivable, and never a stated `state.repo_root` that disagrees with it; the mismatch produces a WARNING naming both paths.
- With an underivable main root (non-git worktree), the documented fallback + warning behaviour is unchanged (existing harness and tests stay green).
- `_record_finish_own_churn` returns only paths inside the finished repo that were observed dirty in that checkout after the fast-forward; foreign, absolute, escaping and not-observed paths are dropped and surfaced as a diagnostic, never allow-listed.
- A refused or no-op fast-forward yields an empty `own_churn`.
- Deletions remain never-allow-listed, and a clean finish still passes with no false-positive abort (SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG).
- All tests from the sibling test item pass on the fixed tree and fail on the pre-fix tree; changed-scope gate green via `/skill:test`.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_resolve_main_repo_root`, `_record_finish_own_churn`, `_main_checkout_guard_violations`, `_fast_forward_local_dev_for_push`, `phase_finish` Step 5/5b.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_cross_checkout_attribution.py`, `test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py`, `test_repo_root_resolution.py`.
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` — attribution/allow-list precedent.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — contract wording owned by the docs item.

## Related work

- SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG (completed) — attribution allow-list precedent; must not regress.
- SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN (blocked) — push from the worktree holding the commit: Step-5 fast-forward + pre-push guard interplay.

## Goal

As a test-value reviewer, I want a cheap static measure of how a test asserts and how much it relies on mocks, so I can pre-filter the suites that mutation testing should examine and give `toHaveBeenCalledWith`-style coupling an enforceable signal.

## Problem statement

`evaluate_usefulness.py` detects only crude anti-patterns (source-grep, placeholder, zero assertions, self-referential). It cannot distinguish a test that asserts observable behaviour from one that asserts internal collaborator calls, nor quantify mock density — yet mock density is a central independent variable in the hypothesis that high-volume mock-heavy suites detect fewer faults. Without this signal, the mutation campaign has no cheap way to choose where to spend its runtime.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Parses TypeScript/JavaScript (and ideally Python) test files and reports per file: assertion count, assertions on internal collaborators vs public behaviour, mock/stub/spy count and ratio, and tests with no meaningful assertion.
- [ ] Flags `toHaveBeenCalledWith`/mock-call assertions on internal collaborators as a distinct, actionable signal (aligned with `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G`).
- [ ] Emits JSON + Markdown with documented definitions and conservative thresholds.
- [ ] Handles dynamic/indirect assertion styles without crashing, and reports uncertainty rather than a false verdict.
- [ ] Runs as a cheap pre-filter (no test execution) and documents that it is a proxy, not ground truth.
- [ ] Covered by tests; all related documentation updated; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Static analysis only; never executes the target project's tests.
- Conservative: uncertainty is reported, never auto-pruned.
- Language-neutral entry point with per-language adapters; no hardcoded project paths.

## Goal

As a maintainer of a large test suite, I want to detect near-duplicate test blocks and files, so additive accumulation can be measured and redundant coverage pruned with evidence.

## Problem statement

The test-churn analysis measured large net test growth (+137,022 lines on the reference project) with a low rewrite ratio — the failure mode is additive accumulation, not churn. `evaluate_usefulness.py`'s "duplicate coverage" check is a heuristic and cannot find near-duplicates introduced through different import paths or copy-paste variation. - [ ] Detects near-duplicate test blocks (within and across files) using normalised AST/token similarity, not raw text matching.

- [ ] Emits JSON + Markdown with thresholds and limitations documented.
- [ ] Performance is bounded on a large suite (documented sampling/scope options).
- [ ] Covered by tests; all related documentation updated; full project test suite passes.

# Intake Brief: Repeat producer actions in red on the final report conclusion

## Problem statement

The canonical end-of-session report (`skill/report`) lists blocking producer
actions in `## Producer Actions`, but the `## Conclusion` — the last thing the
operator reads — does not repeat them. When a session ends with something the
producer must do (answer a question, make a decision, grant an approval), the
operator can miss it in the body of a long report. Repeating any genuine
producer action in the Conclusion in red makes the blocking call-to-action
impossible to overlook.

## Users

- **Producer/operator** reading end-of-session reports in the pi TUI: wants the
  blocking action to stand out at the end of the report, not be buried mid-page.
- **Agent (intake/plan/implement/audit/…) authoring the report**: keeps passing
  blocking actions via `--producer-actions`; the renderer handles the red
  repetition deterministically (no per-skill change).

Example user stories:

- "As a producer, when a skill session needs a decision from me, I want that
  decision repeated in red in the conclusion so I cannot miss it."
- "As a producer, when nothing is required of me, I do not want a red warning in
  the conclusion."
- "As an agent, I want the renderer to do this automatically so every skill
  behaves the same way."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the normalised producer actions are a genuine, non-`None needed`
   action, `render_report()` appends the action text **verbatim** to the
   `## Conclusion` section, wrapped in ANSI SGR red (`\x1b[31m…\x1b[0m`) with a
   `⚠️ Producer action required:` lead-in. Verified by unit test asserting the
   escape sequences and the exact action text inside `## Conclusion`.
2. When no producer actions are supplied, or the supplied text is routine
   workflow progression that normalises to `None needed`, the Conclusion
   contains no ANSI escape sequences and no repeated action text. Verified by
   unit tests (absent actions; `Proceed to /skill:plan`; `Review the brief, then
   run /skill:plan`).
3. Colour can be disabled with a new `--no-colour` CLI flag **or** the standard
   `NO_COLOR` environment variable (non-empty). In that mode the Conclusion
   still repeats the action in plain text with the `⚠️` marker and contains no
   ANSI escape sequences. Verified by unit tests for both opt-outs.
4. Multi-line / multi-action producer text is repeated verbatim (line breaks
   preserved) and the rest of the report is unchanged: section order,
   `## Producer Actions` → `## Notes` → `## Conclusion`, the existing
   completed/incomplete conclusion sentences, and the `</end_session>`
   terminator. Verified by regression tests.
5. `skill/report/SKILL.md` documents the conditional red repetition in the
   canonical template, the layout rules, and the colour opt-out
   (`--no-colour` / `NO_COLOR`) alongside the existing icon opt-out. Verified
   by document review.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Implement in the shared renderer only (`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`)
  plus a small shared colour helper — do not fork report logic into the ~17
  calling skills.
- Repeat **after** routine-next-step normalisation (SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW): a
  routine next step must never produce red text.
- Do not use TTY detection to decide colour: the CLI's stdout is captured/piped
  by agents before being pasted into the final response, so TTY detection would
  disable the feature exactly where it is needed. Opt-out must be explicit
  (`--no-colour` / `NO_COLOR`).
- Colour is decorative: the `⚠️` marker and the plain action text must carry the
  meaning when colour is unavailable, so the report stays readable in
  non-ANSI consumers (GitHub, plain-text logs).
- No new runtime dependency; pure-Python, offline-testable.
- Do not change `## Producer Actions` semantics, the pane-status derivation, or
  the existing conclusion wording.

## Existing state

- `render_report()` renders `## Producer Actions` from the normalised
  `producer_actions` string (`None needed` when absent), then `## Notes`, then
  `## Conclusion`.
- The Conclusion currently emits one of two fixed sentences based on AC
  verdicts (`_derive_session_status`): completed → "This completes … Ready for
  `<next_action>`."; incomplete → "… is incomplete. Requires attention
  (`<next_action>`)." Nothing else is appended.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` already provides `icons_enabled(no_icons, env)`
  honouring `--no-icons` / `WL_NO_ICONS=1` — the convention to mirror for
  colour, but colour must be a separate switch (`WL_NO_ICONS` must not disable
  colour).
- No ANSI/colour handling exists anywhere in the report renderer today (the
  only ANSI in the repo is in `tests/integration/test-worktree-workflow.sh`).

## Desired change

- Add `colour_enabled(no_colour=False, env=None)` (and `RED`/`RESET` constants)
  to `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`: enabled by default; disabled by
  `--no-colour` or a non-empty `NO_COLOR`.
- In `render_report()`, after the existing conclusion sentence(s), when the
  normalised producer actions are not `None needed`, append a blank line and a
  red line: `⚠️ Producer action required: <verbatim action text>`. Apply
  `RED … RESET` only when colour is enabled.
- Thread an optional `no_colour: bool = False` parameter through
  `render_report()`, `render_report_from_workitem()`, `render_from_wl()` and the
  CLI, adding the `--no-colour` flag.
- Update `skill/report/SKILL.md` (template, layout rules, example, colour
  opt-out) and the `README.md` report-helper bullet to mention the red
  repetition.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — conditional red repetition in the
  Conclusion; `no_colour` plumbing and `--no-colour` flag.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` — `colour_enabled()` helper + `RED`/`RESET`
  constants mirroring `icons_enabled()`.
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` — new tests: red repetition,
  no-repetition for absent/routine actions, `--no-colour`/`NO_COLOR` fallback,
  multi-line preservation, structure regression.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_herdr_pane.py` — `colour_enabled()` unit tests.
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` — template/layout/example + colour opt-out docs.
- `README.md` — report-helper bullet: note the red repetition of blocking
  producer actions in the Conclusion.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW** — "Don't include producer actions that are next steps"
  (completed): established normalisation to `None needed`; the red repetition
  must run after it.
- **SA-0MULPQ3BK001A1M5** — "Misleading completion message on LLM summaries"
  (completed): made the Conclusion reflect session status; this item extends the
  same section.
- **SA-0MTFLQEQQ0083EW1** — "Update pane title with status emoticon on skill
  completion" (completed): established the ✅/⚠️/🚫 status colour semantics this
  feature reuses for a red call-to-action.
- **SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S** — "Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting
  via helper report skill" (completed): origin of the canonical report contract.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "red font" means ANSI SGR red in terminal output.** The report
  is rendered to stdout and pasted into the pi TUI; ANSI is the only mechanism
  that reliably colours that path. If the producer expects Markdown/HTML
  colouring, the brief should be revised before implementation (documented in
  the Appendix).
- **Assumption — red repeats blocking actions only.** Because routine workflow
  progression is normalised to `None needed` first, it can never trigger red;
  this avoids the false "producer is blocking" signal fixed by
  SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW.
- **Assumption — no TTY detection.** Explicit opt-out only, because agent-captured
  stdout is not a TTY.
- **Risk — ANSI leakage into non-terminal consumers** (GitHub, PRs, plain logs).
  Mitigation: `--no-colour`/`NO_COLOR`, plus the `⚠️` marker and plain text so the
  meaning survives even if escapes are stripped or shown literally.
- **Risk — colour-blindness / theme contrast.** Mitigation: the `⚠️` marker and
  the words "Producer action required" carry the signal; colour is decorative.
- **Risk — multi-line producer text.** Mitigation: wrap the whole block once and
  test line-break preservation rather than prefixing each line.
- **Scope creep.** Adjacent ideas (colouring the `## Producer Actions` section,
  colourising AC verdicts, HTML-export colour) are out of scope — record as
  separate work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What does 'red font' mean for a Markdown report rendered by the LLM/TUI —
  ANSI escape codes, HTML `<span style=\"color:red\">`, or plain emphasis?"
  — **Answer (repo research + design analysis):** ANSI SGR red. The report is
  printed to stdout and pasted into the terminal-rendered TUI; raw ANSI passes
  through and colours the terminal, whereas inline HTML styles are not honoured
  by the Markdown→terminal path and GitHub strips `style` attributes. Recorded
  as an assumption; the producer can request an HTML/bold variant at review.
  No interactive round was required for the rest of the brief.
- Q: "Should routine next-step actions (e.g. 'Proceed to /skill:plan') also be
  repeated in red?" — **Answer (SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW contract):** No. Routine
  workflow progression is normalised to `None needed` and must never be shown as
  a blocking red action; only genuine, current-stage actions are repeated.
- Q: "Should colour be auto-detected (TTY) or explicitly opt-out?" — **Answer
  (design analysis):** Explicit opt-out only. Agent-captured stdout is not a
  TTY, so TTY detection would silently disable the feature on the exact path
  that needs it. `--no-colour` and `NO_COLOR` are the opt-outs.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVQ1QM9L0083KAW** – Producer Actions contract: docs and skill templates (completed)
- **SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW** – Don't include producer actions that are next steps (completed)
- **SA-0MVRBPVU1001NGDW** – Refactor: Unknown in /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MVQ1QK1R0052WGP-consistency-check-no-next-step-producer/skill/report/scripts/check_producer_actions.py (open)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: action, actions, conclusion, final, llm, producer, red, repeat, them, there
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — matched: action, actions, final, llm, output, producer, red, repeat, them, there
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: action, actions, final, llm, output, producer, red, repeat, them, there

# ship: CHANGELOG release section is discarded by the dev→main merge conflict resolution

**Origin:** observed in the `1916: The Rising` v0.1.23 release (RISE-0MVXXKJGK004WO6L). The Discord release notification went out with no release focus and no changelog body, and `main`'s `CHANGELOG.md` had no `## v0.1.23` section.

## Root cause

In `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` the CHANGELOG is generated **before** `origin/dev` is merged:

1. `generate-changelog.js "$NEW_VERSION"` writes `## v0.1.23 (…)` (with the `> **Release focus:** …` marker) and commits it on the release branch, which is based on `main`.
2. `git merge --no-ff origin/dev` then conflicts on `CHANGELOG.md`, because `dev` carries its own `## Unreleased` block.
3. The auto-resolution runs `git checkout --theirs CHANGELOG.md` — taking dev's whole file and **discarding the generated release section**.
4. The merged tree is tagged, so the released tree carries no `## v<version>` section.

The comment above the resolution (lines 217-219) even claims "generate-changelog.js rewrites it for the new version **afterwards**", contradicting the actual order.

Downstream effects:
- `discord-notify.js` `extractChangelogSection()` returns `null` and `extractReleaseFocus()` finds no marker, so the embed loses both the focus and the release notes (silently — only a focus warning is logged).
- Release notes are absent from `main`/`dev` for that version (recoverable only from the discarded commit).

## Proposed fix

1. Preserve the generated section across the merge: when `CHANGELOG.md` conflicts, take dev's version and then **re-insert** the generated `## v<version>` section (a small, tested helper), instead of discarding it.
2. Assert after the merge that a generated section is still present; abort the release (before tagging) if it was lost. A *failed generation* keeps today's non-fatal behaviour (warn and continue) — this only guards the regression where a successfully generated section is dropped.
3. `discord-notify.js`: log an explicit warning naming the version when no `## v<version>` section is found (still non-blocking).
4. Document the guarantee in `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`.

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/changelog-merge.js` (new helper)
- `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js`
- `skill/ship/tests/test_changelog_merge.mjs` (new)
- `skill/ship/tests/test_discord_notify.mjs`
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`

## Acceptance criteria

1. With dev's `CHANGELOG.md` modified (an `## Unreleased` block present), the merge-resolution path yields a file that contains the generated `## v<version>` section with its `> **Release focus:**` marker **and** keeps dev's content — asserted by a node test over the new merge helper using a dev-style file.
2. When a section was generated but is missing after the merge, the release script aborts before tagging with an actionable message (non-zero exit) — asserted by a test of the resolution helper's "section lost" outcome plus the script-level guard.
3. A failed generation keeps the non-fatal contract: the release continues with an explicit warning, and the guard does not fire for a section that was never generated — asserted by a test.
4. `discord-notify.js` emits an explicit warning naming the version when the `## v<version>` section is absent, and still sends the notification (non-blocking) — unit test with an injected fetch.
5. The Discord embed still carries both the release focus and the changelog body when a generated section is present — unit test on the composition path.
6. `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` documents the ordering/preservation guarantee and the abort-on-loss behaviour.

## Goal

`_git_commit_evidence` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` resolves a
stranded child's pushed-commit evidence with
`git log <ref> --grep <child_id> -n 1`. `--grep` matches the **whole commit
message including the body**, so a commit that merely *mentions* a work-item id
counts as that item's work.

Observed 2026-11-01 during the epic drive for SA-0MVX1M6HH004YPX2: driven child
SA-0MVX359B7008R9F3 timed out after 3600 s with its own commit (`9119e4117`)
still unpushed in its worktree, and `drive` reported it as *stranded* with
evidence `0fb0e4305` — the **sibling** child's (SA-0MVX31GLC002IPR8) commit,
whose body names SA-0MVX359B7008R9F3 as the future home of the detection
module. The verdict told the operator to `--finalise-stranded` a child whose
work had never been pushed.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Commit evidence matches only commits whose **subject** references the
   work-item id, never a body-only mention.
2. A regression test pins the false-positive: a commit whose body mentions
   another item's id is not evidence for that item.
3. A driven child whose commit is still only in its own worktree is reported
   as non-terminal-with-work, not as stranded on the parent branch.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_git_commit_evidence`
- `skill/implement/tests/` — regression test

## Goal (user story)

*As a framework maintainer*, I need the semaphore's slot-**discovery** rule pinned
by unit tests, so a future semaphore change cannot silently reintroduce the
snapshot-ceiling starvation that stalled a test run for 105 minutes
(SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0).

## Context

`Semaphore._try_acquire_slot()` in `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` iterates
`range(self.max_workers)` and `flock`s the first free file. `max_workers` is
resolved once in `__init__`, so a waiter created with `max_workers=2` **never
opens slot files `2..7`**, even when they exist in the namespace and are
unlocked. Live evidence (2026-10-31): `/run/user/1000/pi-semaphores/test/` held
slot files `0`-`7`, slots `2,3,4,6,7` were free, and the waiter owned no lock.

This child adds the **failing-first** unit tests only. The implementation is
child "Semaphore: dynamic slot discovery across the namespace", which removes
the strict `xfail` markers added here.

## Scope (tests only)

File: `skill/shared/tests/test_process_semaphore.py` (hermetic — the existing
`_isolate_lock_dir` autouse fixture already points `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` at
`tmp_path`):

- **Discovery:** a waiter constructed with `max_workers=2` against a namespace
  whose slots `0` and `1` are both held, which has already polled at least
  twice, must acquire within the documented bound (one poll interval plus one
  `flock` attempt) once slot files `2..7` are created and left free.
- **Poll cadence:** the documented maximum poll interval is `1.5 x
  _RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS` = 75 ms with jitter enabled and 50 ms with jitter off;
  pin that no attempt sleeps longer than that cap and that a long-waiting
  consumer performs many attempts (`> 3`), not one.
- **Own-ceiling floor:** a waiter never creates slot files beyond its own
  `max_workers` (only `0..1`), even when higher-index slots exist.
- **Late slot observed across many cycles:** create the new slot only after at
  least three poll cycles and assert the waiter still acquires it.

## Constraints

- Tests are hermetic: temporary `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`, no host-wide pool, no
  reliance on `/run/user`.
- Behaviour that does not exist yet is pinned with
  `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason="SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0 discovery not implemented; marker removed by the implementation child")`
  — repo precedent: `_GATE_XFAIL` in
  `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_gate_failure_reason.py`. The suite must
  stay green.
- No ad-hoc suite invocations — every run goes through `/skill:test`.

## Repo note

The affected code is this repository's framework source, consumed by other
projects via `scripts/install_pi.sh` and the `~/.pi/agent/skills` symlink. Run
`implement.py start SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0` **from this checkout** so the worktree is
a SorraAgents worktree and `wl` resolves the `SA-*` item against this store.


## Key Files

- `skill/shared/tests/test_process_semaphore.py` — new unit regressions.
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — read-only reference (`_try_acquire_slot`, `_ensure_slots`, `_RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS`, `_jittered_retry_delay`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** A unit test starts a `max_workers=2` waiter against a namespace whose slots `0` and `1` are held, lets it poll at least twice, then creates slot files `2..7` free; the waiter acquires one of the new slots well inside its timeout. Marked `xfail(strict=True)` while the fix is absent.
- **AC2** A test pins the maximum poll interval (50 ms base, `[0.5, 1.5]x` jittered, so 75 ms maximum) and asserts a long waiter makes many attempts (`> 3`).
- **AC3** A test asserts a waiter creates no slot files beyond its own `max_workers`.
- **AC4** A test creates the new slot only after at least three poll cycles and asserts the waiter still observes and acquires it.
- **AC5** The new behaviour assertions carry strict `xfail` markers naming this work item; the suite is green (`/skill:test`, changed scope) with the markers in place.
- **AC6** All tests are hermetic (temporary `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`, no host-wide pool) and use no ad-hoc suite invocation.

> The block below restates the parent criteria this child satisfies (parent item
> SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0). It is the machine-checkable coverage mapping, not additional
> child criteria.

### Acceptance Criteria — parent coverage (restated)

- **Parent AC1** — Bounded acquisition once any slot in the namespace is free: a waiter that began polling when only slots 0..N-1 existed must acquire within a documented bound (one poll interval plus one flock attempt) as soon as any slot file in its namespace is free, including slot files created by a later, higher-ceiling process; a max_workers=2 waiter acquires one of the new slots created after it began polling, well inside its timeout.
- **Parent AC2** — Documented maximum poll interval, no unbounded backoff: the poll cadence has a documented maximum interval (50 ms base, jittered 0.5-1.5x when jitter is enabled) and a test pins that a long-waiting consumer still observes slots created after it began waiting (many poll cycles, not one); no backoff may grow without a documented cap.
- **Parent AC4** — Testing/validation: new and updated tests cover AC1 (slot created after the waiter started), AC2 (max interval pinned; late-created slot observed) and AC3 (genuine saturation notice); tests are hermetic (temporary PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR, no host-wide pool) and use real subprocesses where the behaviour is cross-process, with no ad-hoc suite invocations.
data.title: Test: slot-discovery unit regressions for the shared semaphore

## Goal (user story)

*As a producer/release operator*, I need proof that a `slot_busy` verdict means
the pool really was full for the whole wait, and *as a framework maintainer* I
need the cross-process discovery rule pinned, so "the waiter is stuck" can never
be mistaken for "retry later" (SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0).

## Context

Two gaps are unpinned today:

1. **Cross-process discovery.** A low-ceiling waiter (`max_workers=2`) cannot
   use a higher-index slot (`3`) that another process created and left free —
   the defect described in the parent item and reproduced in-process by the
   sibling test child.
2. **Genuine saturation.** `slot_busy` must keep meaning "every slot in the
   namespace was held for the whole `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`", including when the
   namespace contains slots the waiter itself never created. The shipped notice
   (`SLOT_BUSY_NOTICE_PREFIX` / `NOTICE_SLOT_BUSY` = `slot_busy`) must not be
   weakened or renamed — `implement.py`'s finish gate classifies on the code.

## Scope (tests only)

- `skill/shared/tests/test_concurrency_guard.py` — cross-process regression
  with **real subprocesses** (the behaviour is cross-process): the parent
  creates and holds slots `0` and `1`, leaves slot `3` free, then a subprocess
  waiter with `max_workers=2` must acquire slot `3` and exit successfully
  inside a short timeout. A second assertion records the slot files the
  subprocess created and proves it created none above its own `max_workers`.
- `skill/test/tests/test_test_skill_semaphore.py` — extend the saturation
  regression: hold **every** slot present in the namespace (including
  higher indices `2..7` created by the test) with a short `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`,
  then assert `run_suite` still reports the `slot_busy` notice code with the
  existing staggered-retry guidance text unchanged.

## Constraints

- Hermetic: temporary `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` via `nested_semaphore_dir` / fixture
  isolation; no host-wide pool; no ad-hoc suite invocation (use `/skill:test`).
- Discovery assertions are pinned with `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason="SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0 discovery not implemented; marker removed by the implementation child")`
  so the suite stays green until the implementation child lands.
- The saturation assertions must pass **now** — the notice contract must not
  regress.

## Repo note

The affected code is this repository's framework source, consumed by other
projects via `scripts/install_pi.sh` and the `~/.pi/agent/skills` symlink. Run
`implement.py start SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0` **from this checkout** so the worktree is
a SorraAgents worktree and `wl` resolves the `SA-*` item against this store.


## Key Files

- `skill/shared/tests/test_concurrency_guard.py` — cross-process discovery regression.
- `skill/test/tests/test_test_skill_semaphore.py` — genuine-saturation notice regression.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — read-only reference (`_test_concurrency_slot`, `NOTICE_SLOT_BUSY`, `SLOT_BUSY_NOTICE_PREFIX`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** A cross-process test proves a `max_workers=2` subprocess waiter acquires a higher-index slot (`3`) created and left free by another process, well inside its timeout. Marked `xfail(strict=True)` until the fix lands.
- **AC2** A test proves the waiter creates no slot files above its own `max_workers`, cross-process.
- **AC3** With every slot in the namespace held for the whole `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (including higher indices), the test skill still raises `TestConcurrencyTimeout` carrying the `slot_busy` notice code (`NOTICE_SLOT_BUSY` / `SLOT_BUSY_NOTICE_PREFIX`) and the existing staggered-retry guidance — unchanged wording.
- **AC4** Tests are hermetic (temporary `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`, real subprocesses only where the behaviour is cross-process) and run via `/skill:test`, not ad hoc.
- **AC5** The suite is green with the strict `xfail` markers in place.

> The block below restates the parent criteria this child satisfies (parent item
> SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0). It is the machine-checkable coverage mapping, not additional
> child criteria.

### Acceptance Criteria — parent coverage (restated)

- **Parent AC3** — Genuine saturation still reports slot_busy: when every slot in the namespace is held for the whole TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT, the test skill still raises TestConcurrencyTimeout carrying the slot_busy notice code and the existing staggered-retry guidance; the no-slot notice must not be weakened or renamed.
- **Parent AC4** — Testing/validation: new and updated tests cover AC1 (slot created after the waiter started), AC2 (max interval pinned; late-created slot observed) and AC3 (genuine saturation notice); tests are hermetic (temporary PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR, no host-wide pool) and use real subprocesses where the behaviour is cross-process, with no ad-hoc suite invocations.
